text:
anzu: heads-up — onboarding run for orpheus-2 (64k context, int8-opt) produced reproducible drift after ~28k tokens. posting concise triage.
pavan: can you summarise symptoms?
anzu: short: small probability deviations accumulate after rotary rebase window boundary, leading to semantic divergence by ~34k. float16 baseline fine. int8 path shows checksum mismatch at boundary.
arnold: share repro command?
anzu: ```
# repro_longwind.sh
python bench_infer.py --model orpheus-2-int8-opt --context 65536 --prompt tests/long_story_seed.txt --seed 7 --deterministic --no-sampling > /tmp/out.txt
```
mira: what metrics do we track for the bringup?
anzu: we log: token_mismatch_rate, cumsum_token_prob_delta, prefix-rouge, and kv_crc per checkpoint. Current numbers: TMR@32k=0.21%, cumsum_prob_delta +0.087, prefix-rouge drop 0.6.
ciara: kv_crc? any concrete mismatch?
anzu: sample: KV_CRC:28672:0x3b7c9f12 vs baseline 0x3b7c9f12 (match), KV_CRC:32768:0x4f2a1d8b vs baseline 0x4f2a1d8c (off by 1) — appears exactly at 32k rebase.
pavan: off-by-one CRC points at a single element diff; could be rotary table rounding or a write-size/stride edge effect when copying blocks.
arnold: did we try double-precision precompute of sin/cos and then quantize?
anzu: yes — int8 path with double->quant reduced mismatch magnitude but did not eliminate it. drift delayed by ~1500 tokens.
mira: anything else changed in build? new kernel flags or packing?
anzu: kernel ABI same. however, the int8 rotary-kernel was switched to fused interleaved layout last week. suspect quantization & layout interaction.
ci-bot: Canary job created: canary/orpheus-2-int8-opt -> staging-pool-5 at 09:40 UTC.
ciara: can we reproduce on cpu emulation to rule out device packing?
anzu: cpu-emulation reproduces with same seed, though divergence timing varies slightly. implies numerical quantization not DMA packing.
arnold: propose experiments: (A) run fp32-shadow to dump per-token rotary phase applied, (B) instrument KV element-by-element diffs at 4k granularity, (C) run quant-table bitwidth sweep (8->9->10 bits), (D) small layout rollback (pre-fused) to test layout coupling.
pavan: I'll own (A) and (C) on bench cluster. Estimated 2-3 hours.
mira: I'll open a short PR to add element-level KV diff dump and a unit that asserts no more than 1-bit Hamming diff across 64k.
ciara: add a micro-test that replays same seed and fails if TMR > 0.1% before 48k.
anzu: interesting quick test: apply tiny phase offset to rotary at runtime: rotary_phase *= (1.0 + delta). With delta ~ 2e-6 we saw divergence shift linearly. suggests phase quantization sensitivity.
arnold: that result points to rotary quant resolution being critical for long ctx. maybe we need per-block bias compensation when quantizing trig tables.
pavan: running initial fp32-shadow now. I'll post logs to the artifacts bucket.
anzu: artifacts path: s3://redwood-ci/eng-ml/5498765432/ (contains out.txt, kv_crcs.txt, rotary_dumps/, diffs/).
mira: timeline? if fp32-shadow confirms table mismatch, we can ship a quick mitigation: compute trig table at float16 and store as 10-bit quant with per-block scale offsets.
ci-bot: Test run completed: canary/orpheus-2-int8-opt -> passed basic smoke.
ciara: keep in mind production rollout gating: require TMR <0.05% up to 48k in staging.
arnold: longer-term RFC: quant-aware rotary encoding that preserves phase across block boundaries and supports variable kernel layouts. I'll draft.
pavan: fp32-shadow results: rotary_phase at step 32768 differs element #113 by 1.2e-6 relative to baseline; corresponding kv element shows 2 LSB difference after quant. uploading diff.csv to S3.
mira: starting bitwidth sweep: 8-bit baseline, testing 9 and 10 bits for trig table quant. will share perf/accuracy tradeoffs.
anzu: thanks everyone. please tag me on results. i'll compile a triage note and link the artifacts. :rocket:
